## My Thinking

My family has been farming in Quzhou for generations. The land here is flat, the soil is decent loam, and everyone around me grows winter wheat followed by summer maize. That rotation is what I know, what my neighbors do, what the seed dealers stock, and what the grain buyers come to purchase. I'm not going to experiment with something unfamiliar — I have about 12 mu under my management and I need reliable income.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October after preparing the field with a rotary tiller following maize harvest. I'll buy the improved wheat variety the village agronomist recommended last year — something like Jimai 22 or similar — not the expensive hybrid, but certified improved seed. I'll apply diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress urea around jointing stage. Wheat in this area needs water badly — I'll irrigate at sowing if soil is dry, then at jointing, heading, and grain fill. That's three or four times depending on rainfall. I'll spray fungicide once for powdery mildew and aphids once before heading.

For maize, I'll sow directly into the wheat stubble right after the June harvest — no time to till, the season is short. I'll use a hybrid like Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, which everyone uses here. One or two fertilizer applications — base plus a top-dress at V6. Maize here usually gets enough summer rain, so I'll irrigate only once at silking if it's dry. One pesticide spray for corn borer.

I'm not going to overthink this. Same plan as last year, roughly.
